title: Draft: matter: track unsecured conversations, report retransmitted packets
description:
Add conversation tracking for unsecured sessions. Conversations are created
based on UDP endpoint pairs as usual, then a list of sessions is stored in
each conversation. For each session, store a mapping between message
counters and Wireshark frame numbers.

This is currently used to implement two user-visible features: adding a
"session index" to ease filtering a single session (similar to tcp.stream),
and marking duplicated message counters as "retransmitted" linking to the
original frame they are a duplicate of.

I'm using arrays and linear search for simplicity. It's unlikely that a
conversation will have so many sessions, or an unsecured session will have
so many messages, that binary search / tree / hashmap will be worth the
overhead. But I may need to revisit this when implementing secure sessions.

Nitpicks welcome.

notes.body:
Currently I'm creating conversations based on IP:port, and storing a map of "ephemeral initiator node ID -> session" in the conversation. One alternative could be to use the node ID as part of the conversation lookup key, so that each Matter session has a different Wireshark conversation.

However, I had some issues getting that to work with the "conversation element list" API. For example, would I need to do a second lookup with swapped src/dest endpoints to find packets in the opposite direction? Currently that's handled automatically by find_conversation.

It also felt like that approach would cause me problems in the future with secured sessions, which are identified by a "session ID" field, with different value in each direction...

Hrm maybe I should split this into multiple commits, it's kind of adding many things at once :thinking:
I didn't expect all compilers to support this, but if they do, good.
My understanding is an empty initializer wasn't officially added to the C spec until C23, but many compilers support it. I seem to recall at least some erring out in the past. `{0}` is safer.
Is it possible is_initiator won't be set here?
Is it appropriate to look up/update the conversation if this frame has already been visited?
Not sure if this is the right place for this but here is another dissector for matter here https://github.com/project-chip/matter-dissector
